title: console list page: a lookup target object is read twice (presence read, then by name), adding one request layer
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

Filing gate: maintainer ruling on #34211, option A, condition 2 (analysis project file `objectstack-seat5/area-ux/decision-34211.md`). ⛔ Not a claim. Lease `ux-2`.

## What happens (read from code, not yet traced live)

When a list has a lookup field to an object that is outside the package (on the showcase, `sys_user`), the console first asks whether the object exists with one `?names=` read: `servedByName` → `readObjectPresence` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/.../appObjectScope.ts:499-512`, `:522-538`). That answer already carries the definition (`fetchScopeNames`, `MetadataProvider.tsx:1529-1546`). Once the name is answered as served, `readNames(lookups)` (`appObjectScope.ts:800`) asks for it again by name (`fetchScopeName` → `readItem` → `getObjectSchema`, `MetadataProvider.tsx:1472-1474`, `:1031-1038`). The pair came in with PR #34299 (presence read to stop 404s). On the showcase list page this is the trailing request layer; about 0.5 s separates the two reads, and the cause is unknown.

The batch scope is kept apart on purpose (`MetadataProvider.tsx:182-194`: no `sortability` envelope, cannot tell absent from refused). The fix has to keep that distinction.

## Do

Trace it on a real app first (showcase and HotCRM list pages, network panel) and confirm both reads and their order. Then serve the by-name read from the presence answer when it carries everything the by-name path needs, or explain in the PR why it cannot.

## Done when

The list page reads a lookup target once. The layer count before and after is measured on both apps, the absent/refused distinction stays pinned, and #34299's no-404 pin still passes.
